segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: What is your English name?

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.translation: My name is Naomi Stone.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: And in Cherokee.

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.translation: They call me ᏌᎵ.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏌᎵ. ᎣᏂ Ꮎ ᏫᏨᏛ ᏣᏅᏔᏍ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: sali. oni na witsvdv tsanvtas yusdi gehv
segments.translation: ᏌᎵ. What is your last name?

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.translation: They just call me ᏌᎵ.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Where were you born?

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.translation: I am from Greasy.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Where were you born? Born.

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.translation: Probably Stilwell.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Stilwell.

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.text: Ꮎ ᏗᏢ ᏃᏭ Ꮎ ᎤᏪᏘ ᎤᏂᏴᎯᏍᏔᏅ Ꮎ ᎤᎾᏓᏂᎳ. Ꮭ ᏱᎨᎵ ᏃᏭ ᏱᎪᏢ.
segments.transliteration: na ditlv nowu na uweti uniyvhistanv na unadanila. tla yigeli nowu yigotlv.
segments.translation: It's where the old were going to at the nursing home. It's not there anymore.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎾᎾ high school ᎾᎥ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏙᎲ ᎤᏪᏘ High School. Stilwell ᎾᎥ ᏥᎨᎲ.
segments.transliteration: nana high school nav tsigehv dohv uweti High School. Stilwell nav tsigehv.
segments.translation: What about the old high school?

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.translation: Yeah, it really was, wasn't it? That school.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Where did you grow up?

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.translation: At Greasy.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎾᏍ ᎠᏂ Proctor ᏗᏢ ᏥᏩᏂᏁᎳ ᎠᎿ ᎠᎾᏍᏗᏢ
segments.transliteration: nas ani Proctor ditlv tsiwaninela ahna anasditlv
segments.translation: Is that where the Proctors live?

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.text: ᏂᎪᎸ ᏛᏍᏊ ᎣᏣᏛᏅᏏᏙ ᏥᎨᏒ ᎠᏎᏂ ᎦᏅᏓᏗᎲ ᎨᎮ Rock Fence ᏗᏢ ᎤᏍᏗ ᏣᏓᏁᎸ ᎠᎿ ᏗᏩᏁᎶᏂᏙᏅ ᎠᎿ ᏕᏡᎬ. ᎦᏅᏓᏗ ᏝᏍᏊ ᎠᎹ ᏲᎩᏁᎮ, ᎠᏎᏂ Ꮭ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏄᏓᎴ ᏯᏆᏅᏖ.
segments.transliteration: nigolv dvsquu otsadvnvsido tsigesv aseni ganvdadihv gehe Rock Fence ditlv usdi tsadanelv ahna diwanelonidonv ahna detlugv. ganvdadi tlasquu ama yoginehe, aseni tla gohusdi nudale yaquanvte.
segments.translation: We were always moving around. There was a little house towards Rock Fence, and that's where I always played on a little tree.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Where did you get your water?

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.text: uh ᏗᎦᏂᏕᏫᏍᏒ ᎠᎿ ᏗᏢ ᎠᎹ ᏥᎦᏅᎪᎬ ᎢᎦ ᎤᏬᏚ ᎠᎹ ᎤᏴᏜ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᎠᎿ ᏍᏊ ᏥᏙᏨᎩᎶᏍᎬ. ᎠᎹ ᏍᏊ ᎣᎦᏗᏔᏍᏗ ᎠᎿ ᏦᏥᏂᎩᏍᎬ.
segments.transliteration: uh diganidewissv ahna ditlv ama tsiganvgogv iga uwodu ama uyvdla tsigehv. ahna squu tsidotsvgilosgv. ama squu ogaditasdi ahna tsotsinigisgv.
segments.translation: There across the road was really cold and pretty water running. And we were washing clothes there. We were getting our drinking water there.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᎿᏍ ᎤᏩᏒ ᏣᏁᎵᏛ ᏝᎨ ᏄᏓᎴ ᏣᏁᎵᏗᏙᎸ
segments.transliteration: ahnas uwasv tsanelidv tlage nudale tsanelididolv
segments.translation: Is that the only place you lived or have you lived anywhere else?

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.text: uh huh ᏃᎴ ᏓᎳᏂᎩ ᏗᏢ ᏞᎦ ᏥᏬᎦᏁᎸᏛ. ᏃᎴ Malloy Hollow ᏗᏢ. ᏃᏭ ᎡᎵᏭᏛ ᏍᏊ ᏃᏭᏅ ᏅᎩᏚᏢ ᏃᏆᏕᏘᏴᏓ ᎨᎮ ᏃᏭ ᏥᎾᏩᏛᎾᏔᏅ Sequoyah. ᏃᏭ ᏣᎩᏁᎪᏨ ᏥᏓᎩᏍᏆᏛ ᎠᎿ ᏃᏭ ᏓᎵᏆ ᏥᏥᏁᎸ
segments.transliteration: uh huh nole dalanigi ditlv tlega tsiwoganelvdv. nole Malloy Hollow ditlv. nowu eliwudv squu nowunv nvgidutlv noquadetiyvda gehe nowu tsinawadvnatanv Sequoyah. nowu tsaginegotsv tsidagisquadv ahna nowu daliqua tsitsinelv
segments.translation: Uh huh. Then I moved to Dahlonegah. Then to Malloy Hollow. When I was fourteen I started going to Sequoyah. When I graduated from Sequoyah I stayed in Tahlequah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Are you still living in Tahlequah?

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.translation: Uh-huh.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: How many brothers and sisters do you have?

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.text: ᎦᎵᏉᎩ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᏭ ᏅᎩ ᏅᎩ Ꭴ ᏃᏥ ᎣᏥ
segments.transliteration: galiquogi tsigehv nowu nvgi nvgi u notsi otsi
segments.translation: There was seven, but now there is only four left.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏅᎩ ᎢᏥ. Hubert ᎢᏍ ᏣᏚᏥ ᎨᎮ?
segments.transliteration: nvgi itsi. Hubert is tsadutsi gehe?
segments.translation: There's four of you. Was Hubert your uncle?

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.text: huh uh ᎥᎩᏙ. ᎢᎦ ᏍᏊ ᎤᏬᎵᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᎠᏓᏰᏍᎦ ᏥᏄᏥᏓᏁᎸ.
segments.transliteration: huh uh vgido. iga squu uwolidi tsigehv. adayesga tsinutsidanelv.
segments.translation: My brother. He was funny. He had cancer.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Were they all Cherokee speakers?

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.text: Well, ᏣᎳᎩ ᎠᎫᏏ. Ꮎ ᎫᏏ ᎨᎲ ᎢᎦᏓ ᏱᎾᏕᏥᏩ
segments.transliteration: Well, tsalagi agusi. na gusi gehv igada yinadetsiwa
segments.translation: Well, Cherokee and Creek. In Creek I can barely speak.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Did the others speak?

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.text: Yeah, ᏂᎦᏓ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎣᏥᏬᏂᏍᎩ ᏥᎨᏒ ᎫᏐ. ᎠᏆᎨᏫᏍᎨ ᏃᏭ. ᏣᎳᎩ ᏱᏥᏬᏂ ᏍᏗᎩᏓ ᎠᏆᎨᏫᏍᎬ ᏃᏭ ᎾᏆᎵᏍᏓᏁᎰ.
segments.transliteration: Yeah, nigada osda otsiwonisgi tsigesv guso. aquagewisge nowu. tsalagi yitsiwoni sdigida aquagewisgv nowu naqualisdaneho.
segments.translation: We could all speak Creek really good. I'm forgetting it now. I can speak Cherokee, but I'm forgetting it now.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Were they raised same place you were?

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.text: Yeah. Well, ᎠᎭᏂ ᏗᏢ ᏥᎾᏩᏛᏁᏔᏅ ᏧᎾᏕᎶᏆᏍᏗ Ꮟ ᏣᏛᏁᎲᏩ. ᏃᏭ ᏥᏛᏁᏕᎶᏒ ᏨᎨᏒ ᏣᏩᎵᏍᏕᎸᎲ. ᏃᏭ ᏅᏁᎲᏂ Ꮭ ᏯᏁᏃ. ᎾᏛ ᏦᏍᏓᏓᎸ pepsi ᎠᏃᏎᎰ ᎯᏲᎵᎩᏍ? ᏍᎨᏲ Ꮟ Cherry Tree ᏏᏤ
segments.transliteration: Yeah. Well, ahani ditlv tsinawadvnetanv tsunadeloquasdi si tsadvnehvwa. nowu tsidvnedelosv tsvgesv tsawalisdelvhv. nowu nvnehvni tla yaneno. nadv tsosdadalv pepsi anoseho hiyoligis? sgeyo si Cherry Tree sitse
segments.translation: When I went to school they were still living there. When they got sick, I went back home. And then they passed and now they're passed. My sister Pepsi, do you know her? She still lives in Cherry Tree.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Sundown is her husband.

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.text: ᎠᎿᎮN ᏱᏬᏪᏙᎸ ᏣᎳᎩ ᎣᏥᏬᏂᏍᎪ. ᎠᎭᏂ ᏗᏢ ᏥᎨᏙᎲ (???)
segments.transliteration: ahnaheN yiwowedolv tsalagi otsiwonisgo. ahani ditlv tsigedohv (???)
segments.translation: When I go there, we talk Cherokee.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Do you miss speaking Cherokee?

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.text: ᏍᏊᏛᏅ ᏍᎩᎮᏂ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏣᎩᎸᏉᏗ ᎠᎭᏂ ᏓᎩᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎲ.
segments.transliteration: squudvnv sgiheni yusdi tsagilvquodi ahani dagilvwisdanehv.
segments.translation: Yes, that's why I like working here.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Are you working here?

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.text: ᎾᏛ ᏧᏂᏍᏗ ᎤᏂᏴᏍᏗ ᏫᏛᎬᏩᏂᏔᏂ ᏑᎾᎴ ᏣᎾᏗ. ᎣᏍᏓ ᎦᏛ ᎨᎮᏍᏗ ᏅᎩ ᏳᎾᏕᏘᏴᏓ.
segments.transliteration: nadv tsunisdi uniyvsdi widvgvwanitani sunale tsanadi. osda gadv gehesdi nvgi yunadetiyvda.
segments.translation: They said they're going to put me in the baby class. They're going to put me with the four year olds and it's going to be good.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᎿᏩᏍᎪᏅ ᏂᎦᏓ ᏥᎦᏛᏛᎲᏍᎦ ᎠᎿᏩᏍᎪ Ꮟ ᏂᎦᏓ ᎢᏥᏁᎳ
segments.transliteration: ahnawasgonv nigada tsigadvdvhvsga ahnawasgo si nigada itsinela
segments.translation: Is that where all of you were staying? Do you all still live there?

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.translation: Yep, it was a little house and we had a lot of beds.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Grandma and Grandpa, what were their names?

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.text: ᎠᎩᎵᏏᏛ lenny beaver ᎠᎩᏚᏗ josiah vann ᏃᎴᏅ clan beaver ᎠᏎᏅ ᎠᏋᎨᏫᏍᎪ ᏂᎦᏓ ᏚᎾᏙᎥ ᎨᎲ. ᎠᏂᎫᏐᎮᏂ ᏍᏈᏍᏗ ᏥᏄᏍᏛ Ꮎ family tree.
segments.transliteration: agilisidv lenny beaver agidudi josiah vann nolenv clan beaver asenv aquvgewisgo nigada dunadov gehv. anigusoheni squisdi tsinusdv na family tree.
segments.translation: Although, I forget the names of all of them. There were a lot of them that were Creek.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Is Soldier your uncle?

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.translation: He's still alive. He doesn't drive anymore.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Not anymore?

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.translation: Uh-uh.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Why? Is it because he's sick?

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.translation: I guess it's because he's sick.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Sometimes I see him walking.

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.translation: Yeah, they all say they see him walking.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Remembering what kind of foods y'all found?

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.text: ᏂᎪᎸᏛ ᎤᏔᏂ ᏧᏂᏫᏒᏅ ᏂᎦᏓ ᏦᏥᏲᏟ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᎤᎿ ᏗᏢ ᏦᎩᎸᏫᏍᏓᏅᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᏳᏓᎭᏅ ᎾᏩᏚᎵᎮᏅ ᏱᎩ ᏱᏓᎩᏍᎦᏢᎦ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᏎᎷ ᏙᏥᏫᏍᎬ. ᎢᎦ Ꮫ ᏥᎾᎵ ᎨᎮ.
segments.transliteration: nigolvdv utani tsuniwisvnv nigada tsotsiyotli nigohilv uhna ditlv tsogilvwisdanvdi tsigehv. yudahanv nawadulihenv yigi yidagisgatlvga tsigehv na selu dotsiwisgv. iga dv tsinali gehe.
segments.translation: We had a big garden and all of us kids would always help. Sometimes I would hide when we were planting the corn, because I didn't want to help. I was really lazy.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏕᏣᏙD ᏂᎨᎲᏂ ᏱᎩ ᎦᏙ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎠᎾᏗᎮ nickname ᏣᏃᏎᎰ.
segments.transliteration: detsadoD nigehvni yigi gado usdi anadihe nickname tsanoseho.
segments.translation: What other name did they call you besides your real name?

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.text: ᏣᏁᏅ. ᎠᏎᏅ ᎠᎫᏍᏗ ᎮᏂ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏓᏩᏙD.
segments.transliteration: tsanenv. asenv agusdi heni sgina dawadoD.
segments.translation: ᏓᏩᏙD that's my Creek name.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏣᏅᏔᏍ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎦᎦᏓ ᏝᏍ Ᏺ ᏱᏣᏅᏔ
segments.transliteration: tsanvtas yusdi gagada tlas yo yitsanvta
segments.translation: Do you know the meaning? Oh, so you don't know.

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.text: ᎢᎦᏕᎮᏂ Ꮟ ᎫᏐ ᎬᏩᏝᏃᎨᏙ ᎠᎭᏂ ᏥᏓᎩᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎭ ᎫᏐ ᎬᏩᏝᏃᎮᏙ. ᎨᏍᏗ ᏛᏱᎦᏅᏓᏗ ᎦᏥᏲᏎᎰ. Aw, ᏣᏁᏅ ᏱᎬᏬᏎ. ᎮᏍᏗ ᏥᏣᎨᏫᏏ ᏣᏬᏎᎲ David
segments.transliteration: igadeheni si guso gvwatlanogedo ahani tsidagilvwisdaneha guso gvwatlanohedo. gesdi dvyiganvdadi gatsiyoseho. Aw, tsanenv yigvwose. hesdi tsitsagewisi tsawosehv David
segments.translation: Some of the people still want to talk Creek to me since I've been working here and they talk Creek to me. I tell them I don't remember it. They just say "Aw, Janen." David said not to forget it.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Ꮎ Hubert ᏥᏣᏁᏍᏔᏅ ᎤᏬᎵᏗ ᎠᏂᏃᎮᏍᎬ ᎨᎲ ᏌᏊ ᏳᏩᎦᏗ bird eggs ᏣᏃᎮᎲ Ꮎ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏣᏅᏔᏅᏍᎬ. ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ ᎣᏥᏅᏒ Hubert Ꮭ ᎠᏁᏙᎲ bird eggs ᏭᏁᎪᏨ. Ꮭ ᏯᏴᏟᎯᎮ ᎩᎶ ᎣᏣᏛᏛᏅ ᏭᎦᏛᏗ ᏫᎾᏛᏁᎲ Hubert ᎣᏦᎮᎸ. ᎤᏴᏟᏢ Ꮩ ᎭᏛᏁᎮ ᎢᏡᎬ Ꮎ ᏭᎩᎴ ᏧᏪᏥ ᏫᏚᏲᎮ.
segments.transliteration: na Hubert tsitsanestanv uwolidi aninohesgv gehv saquu yuwagadi bird eggs tsanohehv na gohusdi tsanvtanvsgv. sgiyusdi otsinvsv Hubert tla anedohv bird eggs wunegotsv. tla yayvtlihihe gilo otsadvdvnv wugadvdi winadvnehv Hubert otsohelv. uyvtlitlv do hadvnehe itlugv na wugile tsuwetsi widuyohe.
segments.translation: We were talking about Hubert and he was really funny. They were talking about hanging bird eggs. They asked him to get some bird eggs and he just went outside. He wasn't coming in and they asked someone to go out there and see what he was doing. They asked him what he was doing and he said he was outside on a tree looking for bird eggs.

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏛ ᏱᏛᏁ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏬᎵᏗ ᎮᏂ ᎡᏙᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᏙᏍᏊ ᏥᏅᏗᎰ
segments.transliteration: sgidv yidvne tsigehv uwolidi heni edoda tsigehv. dosquu tsinvdiho
segments.translation: That's what he was always doing. He was funny. I miss him.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Yeah, ᎠᏯᏛᏍᏊ ᎣᎩᎾᎵ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᎯᎢᎾ ᏥᏂᏃᎲᎵ Hubert Ꮭ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏯᏅᏓᏗᏍᎪ ᏄᏍᏛ ᎤᏂᏃᎮᏢᏅ ᏕᏣᎦᏴᎵᎨ. ᏣᎵᏏ ᎴᏱᎩ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏣᏰᎸ ᏣᎸᏉᏗ ᏣᏃᎮᏗ.
segments.transliteration: Yeah, ayadvsquu oginali tsigehv. hiina tsininohvli Hubert tla gohusdi yanvdadisgo nusdv uninohetlvnv detsagayvlige. tsalisi leyigi osda tsayelv tsalvquodi tsanohedi.
segments.translation: Me too. He was my friend. Since we're talking about Hubert did they ever talk about anything that was happening a long time ago? Do you want to talk about your grandmother and the good times?

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.text: Well, Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏲᏁᎦ ᎦᎾᎦᏘ ᎤᏪᏓᏍᏗ ᏱᎨᎮ. Ꮎ ᎤᏅᏖ ᎦᎾᎦᏗ ᏛᎮ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎨᎮ. ᏍᎩᏛ ᎯᏳᏍᏗ ᎨᎮ ᏃᏭ Ꮎ ᎦᎾᎦᏘ ᎡᏓᎵᏍᎦᏱᏍᏙᏗ ᏣᏂᏗᎲ
segments.transliteration: Well, tla ilvhiyu yonega ganagati uwedasdi yigehe. na unvte ganagadi dvhe yusdi gehe. sgidv hiyusdi gehe nowu na ganagati edalisgayisdodi tsanidihv
segments.translation: We never had to go to the doctor. I guess she was kind of like an Indian doctor. And now we have to depend on the regular doctors.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: So, ᎢᎾᎨ ᎡᎯ ᏅᏬᏘ ᎠᏂᏗᎮ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᏒ. Ꮭ ᏱᏧᏖᏎ ᎢᎦᏓ Ꮭ ᎯᎦᏔᎭ ᎢᎦᏓ ᏍᎩᎾ. ᎮᏍᏗᎧ ᏱᎫᏖᏏ Ᏺ ᎠᏯ ᎣᏍᏓᎮᏂ ᏱᎨᏎ.
segments.transliteration: So, inage ehi nvwoti anidihe nahiyu tsigesv. tla yitsutese igada tla higataha igada sgina. hesdika yigutesi yo aya osdaheni yigese.
segments.translation: So they only used Indian medicine back then. So you didn't pick it up or learn? We didn't , but it would've been good if we would have.

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.translation: That would have been good.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: It would have been good if we had learned it.

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.text: ᎠᏎᏅ ᎤᏁᏝᏅᎮᏂ ᏥᎵᏍᎦᏍᏛᏂ ᎤᏓᏅᏔ ᏳᏍᏙ ᎨᎲ ᎠᎩᏍᏕᎵᎰ
segments.transliteration: asenv unetlanvheni tsilisgasdvni udanvta yusdo gehv agisdeliho
segments.translation: I leave it up to God. He's very kind. He helps me with everything.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎦᏙ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎢᏣᏛᏁᎮ ᏙᏲᏣᏁᎶᏅ ᏱᏤᎵᏍ ᎦᏙ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎢᏣᏛᏁᎮ ᎾᎯᏳ. ᎮᏍᏗ Ᏺ ᎪᎯᎦ ᏱᎩ ᏥᎾᎾᏛᏁᎰ ᎢᏳᏍᏗ ᎪᎯᏥᎩ
segments.transliteration: gado usdi itsadvnehe doyotsanelonv yitselis gado usdi itsadvnehe nahiyu. hesdi yo gohiga yigi tsinanadvneho iyusdi gohitsigi
segments.translation: How did you all play back then? They don't play like they used to back then.

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.text: ᏙᏛᏲ Glenda Mink ᎾᎥ ᏣᏂᏁᎸ Ꮎ Frank ᏂᎦᏓ. ᏍᎩᎮ ᎢᎦ ᏳᏄᎵᏍᏔᏂ ᏙᏱ ᏦᏍᏗᏅᎪᎦ. ᏱᏙᏍᏓᏁᏲᎲᎦ ᏥᎨᏒ ᎢᎾᎨ ᏳᏬᏍᏗᎶ ᎮᎵᏭ ᎮᏂ ᎧᏄᎦᎵᏗ Ꮎ ᎫᏩᏯ ᏱᏭᏙᏍᏗᎦ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎾᎴ ᏱᎩ ᎤᏫᏒᏅ ᏱᏬᏍᏗᏴ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᏃᎴ ᏧᏙᎵᏗ ᎢᎾᎨ ᏳᏙᏍᏔᏁᎶᎲᎦ ᎢᎾᎨ
segments.transliteration: dodvyo Glenda Mink nav tsaninelv na Frank nigada. sgihe iga yunulistani doyi tsosdinvgoga. yidosdaneyohvga tsigesv inage yuwosdilo heliwu heni kanugalidi na guwaya yiwudosdiga tsigehv nale yigi uwisvnv yiwosdiyv tsigehv. nole tsudolidi inage yudostanelohvga inage
segments.translation: Yes, really. Glenda Mink and Frank lived by us. When it became daylight we came outside. We would go out in the woods and play. We would go out and get some blueberries and blackberries. We would get in the garden. Me and Judohld would play out in the woods.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Were there a lot of you sometimes?

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.text: ᏝᏙ ᏝᏢ ᎣᏤᏙ ᏱᎨᎮ ᎾᎯᏳ. ᏝᏍᏊ ᏱᎾᏙᎩᎾ Ꮎ ᏥᏚᏂᎳᏫᏑᏠ ᏂᎪᎸ ᎢᎾᎨ ᎣᏍᏕᏙ ᏥᎨᎲ.
segments.transliteration: tlado tlatlv otsedo yigehe nahiyu. tlasquu yinadogina na tsidunilawisutlo nigolv inage osdedo tsigehv.
segments.translation: We didn't go anywhere back then. We didn't wear shoes, we were always playing in the woods.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: What about playing ball? Did you ever play ball?

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.translation: When I was in school. I didn't like it.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: You didn't like to play ball?

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.text: ᏝᏛ ᏲᏁᎦ ᏱᏣᎦᏔᎮ ᏝᏙ ᏯᏆᏅᏖ ᏂᎬᎩᏪᏎᎲ ᏧᎾᏕᎶᏆᏍᏗ.
segments.transliteration: tladv yonega yitsagatahe tlado yaquanvte nigvgiwesehv tsunadeloquasdi.
segments.translation: I didn't understand English, so I didn't know what they were saying to me at school.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎾᎾ ᎪᎯ ᏥᏍᎩᏃᏎᎲ Mrs. Eads ᏥᏍᎩᏃᎯᏏ
segments.transliteration: nana gohi tsisginosehv Mrs. Eads tsisginohisi
segments.translation: Tell me about what Mrs. Eads was doing to you all.

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.text: ᎢᎦᏓ ᎤᎾᎸ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏝᏍᏊ ᏯᎩᎸᏉᏗ ᏗᏩᏕᎶᏆᏍᏗ. ᏃᏭ Ꮭ ᏯᏆᏅᏖ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎾᎩᏪᏎᎲ ᏲᏁᎦᎮN ᏣᏩᏝᏃᎮᏗᎮ. ᏃᏊ Ꮭ ᎫᏍᏗ ᏃᎴ ᏴᎩᎸᎩ ᏃᎴ ᏣᎳᎩ ᏃᎴ ᏴᎩᎸᎩ ᏥᎨᏒ. Ꮭ ᏯᎩᎸᏉᏕ ᏗᏩᏕᎶᏆᏍᏗ
segments.transliteration: igada unalv tsigehv tlasquu yagilvquodi diwadeloquasdi. nowu tla yaquanvte yusdi nagiwesehv yonegaheN tsawatlanohedihe. noquu tla gusdi nole yvgilvgi nole tsalagi nole yvgilvgi tsigesv. tla yagilvquode diwadeloquasdi
segments.translation: She was mean. I didn't like to go to school. I didn't understand what she was saying in English. I wouldn't say anything and then she would paddle me and then I would speak Cherokee and then she'd paddle me again. I didn't like school.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: So you weren't allowed to speak Cherokee?

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.translation: We've all been through that.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᏯᏛ Ᏺ ᎮᏍᏗ ᎥᎦᏍᎦᎦ ᏱᎨᎮ Udell ᎮᏂ ᏗᏇᏲᎲᏍᎦ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᎦᎵ ᎠᏎ ᎤᏂᎩᏓ ᎨᏎ Udell ᏂᎯ ᏥᏕᎭᏕᏆᏍᎬ. ᎢᎦᏓᎮᏂ ᎠᏯ ᏗᎬᏪᏲᏅ Mrs King Mrs Spriers and Mrs Campbell Mrs Reed Udell ᏗᎬᏪᏲᏅ ᎠᏯ
segments.transliteration: ayadv yo hesdi vgasgaga yigehe Udell heni diqueyohvsga tsigehv. gali ase unigida gese Udell nihi tsidehadequasgv. igadaheni aya digvweyonv Mrs King Mrs Spriers and Mrs Campbell Mrs Reed Udell digvweyonv aya
segments.translation: They let me speak Cherokee. Udell was my teacher. Udell had already left when you started school. They were all my teachers.

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.translation: Were they nice?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎤᎾᏓᏅᏛ Ᏺ Udell ᏗᏥᏆᎸᏗ ᎤᏓᏅᏔ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: unadanvdv yo Udell ditsiqualvdi udanvta tsigehv
segments.translation: Udell was very nice.

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.text: ᎾᏃ Ꮠ ᎦᏅᏓᏗ Mrs Bolin ᏧᏙᎢᏓ ᏥᏥᏍᎦᏱᎲ ᏍᏊ ᏍᎩᎾ. Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᎠᏆᏕᎳᎰᏒ ᏱᎨᎮ Ꮎ ᏕᎦᎾᏙᎦ ᏱᏕᎦᎴᎩ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᏥᏍᎩᎵᏛ ᏥᎨᎵᎲ. ᏙᎨᏲ ᎤᎵᏍᏓᏁ ᏥᎨᎵᎲ ᏍᎨᏲ ᎤᏁᎫᏥᏓᏍᏊ ᏥᎨᎲ.
segments.transliteration: nano so ganvdadi Mrs Bolin tsudoida tsitsisgayihv squu sgina. tla ilvhiyu aquadelahosv yigehe na deganadoga yidegalegi tsigehv. tsisgilidv tsigelihv. dogeyo ulisdane tsigelihv sgeyo unegutsidasquu tsigehv.
segments.translation: I remember Mrs Bolin. I was afraid of her. I never knew she could probably take her teeth out. I thought she was a booger. I was wondering what was wrong with her. She was mean, too.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏏᏍ Ꮓ Mrs Mays superintendent ᎨᎮ ᏥᏕᎭᏕᎶᏆᏍᎬ
segments.transliteration: sis no Mrs Mays superintendent gehe tsidehadeloquasgv
segments.translation: Was Mrs Mays the superintendent when you were in school?

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.text: ᏝᎰᏩ ᏥᎪᏩᏘᏍᎬ ᏱᎨᎮ. ᏞᏍᏗᎮᏂ ᏍᏊ ᎰᏩ ᏱᏓᏩᏕᎶᏆᎠ ᏱᎨᎵ. ᎢᎦᎡ Ꮭ ᏯᎩᎸᏉᏗ ᎾᏛᎮ ᎥᎩᎸᏂᎲ
segments.transliteration: tlahowa tsigowatisgv yigehe. tlesdiheni squu howa yidawadeloquaa yigeli. igae tla yagilvquodi nadvhe vgilvnihv
segments.translation: I didn't hardly see her. I don't think I went to school very much. I didn't like going to school, I guess because they were always paddling me.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᏯᏛ ᏂᎪᎸᎮᏂ ᎠᎬᏱ ᏗᏢ ᏥᏙᎩᏂᏍᏛᏡᏍᏛ Randy Sanders ᎣᎩᏁᏂᎫᏣ
segments.transliteration: ayadv nigolvheni agvyi ditlv tsidoginisdvtlusdv Randy Sanders oginenigutsa
segments.translation: They always sat me and Randy Sanders in the front because we were mean.

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.translation: Did you like it?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: I didn't like to go to school.

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.text: ᏍᏓᏱ ᎮᏂ ᎠᏕᎶᏆᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏲᏁᎦ ᏙᎲ ᏥᎾᏩᎵᏍᏓᏁᎲ ᎠᏯ ᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: sdayi heni adeloquasdi tsigehv yonega dohv tsinawalisdanehv aya gehv
segments.translation: It was hard to learn English, wasn't it? Well, it seemed like it to me.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: I was too lazy to get up.

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.text: ᎠᏯᏛ Ᏺ ᏍᏓᏱ ᏥᎾᏩᎵᏍᏓᏁᎲ ᏲᏁᎦ ᎾᎾ ᎠᎩᏥ Ꮭ ᏲᏁᎦ ᏯᎦᏔᎮ. ᏍᎩ ᎫᏐ ᏣᎳᎩ ᏣᏂᏬᏂᎲ ᏂᎪᎸ. ᏃᏭ ᏲᏁᎦ Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏲᏁᎦ ᎦᏛᎩᏍᎦ ᏱᎨᎮ. ᏃᏭ ᏥᎩ Ꮭ ᎰᏩ ᏣᎳᎩ ᎦᏛᎩᏍ ᏱᎩ
segments.transliteration: ayadv yo sdayi tsinawalisdanehv yonega nana agitsi tla yonega yagatahe. sgi guso tsalagi tsaniwonihv nigolv. nowu yonega tla ilvhiyu yonega gadvgisga yigehe. nowu tsigi tla howa tsalagi gadvgis yigi
segments.translation: It was hard for me to learn English and my mom didn't know how to speak English. They only spoke Creek and Cherokee. I never did hear English. And now I don't hardly hear Cherokee.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Ꮎ Elm Tree ᏥᎩ ᎣᏏᏍᎩ ᏱᎦ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎪ
segments.transliteration: na Elm Tree tsigi osisgi yiga aniwonisgo
segments.translation: Do they talk plenty of Cherokee at Elm Tree?

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.text: Ꭵ ᎾᎾ ᏙᏓᏩᏍᎬ Bible class ᎥᎿ yeah
segments.transliteration: v nana dodawasgv Bible class vhna yeah
segments.translation: Yes, in Bible class.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: In Cherokee?

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.text: ᎠᏎᏂ ᏢᏍᎩ ᏱᎦ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎩ ᏯᏁᏙᎰ. DJ, Francis, Chris, ᎾᏅ Durbin ᎤᏍᏓᏂᏙᎸ ᏗᎾᏓᎸ. ᏍᏊᎢᎦ ᎨᎵ.
segments.transliteration: aseni tlvsgi yiga aniwonisgi yanedoho. DJ, Francis, Chris, nanv Durbin usdanidolv dinadalv. squuiga geli.
segments.translation: Yeah, there's not that many speakers that come there. DJ, Francis, Chris, and Durbin's wife's sister. I think that's it.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᏯᎮᏂ Belfonte ᏕᏥᎦᏘᏯ ᏙᏓᏩᏍᎬ ᏦᏍᎪ ᏥᏃᏥᎥ ᏂᎦᏗ ᏣᎳᎩ ᎣᏥᏬᏂᏍᎩ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: ayaheni Belfonte detsigatiya dodawasgv tsosgo tsinotsiv nigadi tsalagi otsiwonisgi tsigehv
segments.translation: I'm pastoring Belfonte. We had thirty people on Sunday, all Cherokee speakers.

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.text: Ah, ᎣᏍᏓ ᏍᎩᏛ ᏣᎩᏲᎲ ᏧᏂᎳᏫᏍᏗ ᎡᏍᎦᏂ
segments.transliteration: Ah, osda sgidv tsagiyohv tsunilawisdi esgani
segments.translation: That's what I was looking for. Something close.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: When it's like that, I preach Cherokee.

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.translation: That's good. I might come up there.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Come, come.

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.text: ᎥᎿᏛ coon ᏥᏛᎦᏁᎸ ᎥᎿ ᎠᏪᏓᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᏒ ᎨᎵ
segments.transliteration: vhnadv coon tsidvganelv vhna awedasdi tsigesv geli
segments.translation: That's where Coon lived. I think that's where I was going.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᎿᏛ ᎩᎳ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏍᏓᏯᎲᏍᎦ ᎮᏂ Ꮟ ᎨᎳᏅ
segments.transliteration: ahnadv gila tsigehv usdayahvsga heni si gelanv
segments.translation: He used to be a member, but his wife is still there.

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.translation: Oh, that's good. Tell her I said hi.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎭᏩ. ᎠᎿᎢᏍ Ᏺ ᎠᏂ Proctor ᏫᏣᏁᎳᏛ ᏱᎨᏎ ᎠᎿᏍ Ᏺ. ᏓᎦ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏥᏓᏂᏁᎳ
segments.transliteration: hawa. ahnais yo ani Proctor witsaneladv yigese ahnas yo. daga tsigehv tsidaninela
segments.translation: Did you all live over there? Dag lived over there.

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.text: ᏏᏛ ᏂᎦᏓ ᏗᏂᏁᎳ ᎠᎿ Leroy Ꮎ John ᏧᏲᎱᏒ. Danny Ꭱ
segments.transliteration: sidv nigada dininela ahna Leroy na John tsuyohusv. Danny e
segments.translation: They all still live there, but John passed away. And Danny.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Ꮭ ᏯᏆᏅᏔ ᏝᏃ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎦᏁᎳ Killer Mountain ᏥᏩTLᏍᏗ ᏣᏓᏁᎳ ᎤᏔᎾ ᏝᏍᏊ ᎠᎿ ᏱᏥᏁᎵ ᎾᎨ ᎤᎬᏫᏳᏎ
segments.transliteration: tla yaquanvta tlano sgina ganela Killer Mountain tsiwaTLsdi tsadanela utana tlasquu ahna yitsineli nage ugvwiyuse
segments.translation: I don't know who lives where the Killer Mountain turnoff is. Did you live in the big house across the road?

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.translation: Martha. Martha ᎢᏍ

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Uh-uh.

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.translation: What do you call it?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: That's what you call Highway 59.

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.translation: I don't remember it.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎾᎴ ᏳᎬᏫᏳ Hubert Soldier ᎤᏪᏘ ᎤᏪᏘᎮᏂ ᏣᏓᏁᎳ. ᎠᎿ ᎩᎶᎮᏂ ᏦᏧᏖᏍᏗᎲ
segments.transliteration: nale yugvwiyu Hubert Soldier uweti uwetiheni tsadanela. ahna giloheni tsotsutesdihv
segments.translation: It might've been Hubert or Soldier. It was an old house. We would pick someone up there.

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.text: ᎡᎵᏳᏛ Soldier ᎨᎮ. Yeah, Ꮭ ᏱᎦᏅᏓᏗ
segments.transliteration: eliyudv Soldier gehe. Yeah, tla yiganvdadi
segments.translation: It was probably Soldier. Yeah, I don't remember.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎦᏙ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎭᏅᏓᏗᎰ ᏗᏣᏛᏒ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏣᎪᎥ
segments.transliteration: gado usdi hanvdadiho ditsadvsv yusdi tsagov
segments.translation: What do you remember growing up, the things you saw?

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.text: ᎢᎦᏓ ᎡᏲ ᏂᎪᎸ ᎢᎾᎨ ᏥᏙᏍᏓᏁᎶᎲᏍᎬ. ᎢᎦ ᏳᏍᏙ ᎮᎲ ᎤᏬᏚᎯ ᏥᎾᏩᎵᏍᏓᏁᎲ. ᏃᏭ school ᏗᏢ ᎠᏪᏅᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏩᏓᏂᎵ ᏱᏥᏲᏎ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᎢᎾᎨ ᏗᏢ ᎠᏪᏅᏍᏗ ᏣᏩᏚᎵᎲ. ᎣᏍᏓ ᏃᎦᏛᏅ ᏥᎨᎵᎲ ᏝᏍᏊ ᏙᏳ ᎤᏁᏓᏍᏗ ᏱᏃᎬᏁ ᏲᎪᏢᏎ ᏝᏍᏊ ᎠᎹ ᏗᎦᎷᎦ ᏱᎨᎮ ᎠᏎᏂ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏥᎨᎵᎲ.
segments.transliteration: igada eyo nigolv inage tsidosdanelohvsgv. iga yusdo hehv uwoduhi tsinawalisdanehv. nowu school ditlv awenvsdi tsigehv awadanili yitsiyose tsigehv. inage ditlv awenvsdi tsawadulihv. osda nogadvnv tsigelihv tlasquu doyu unedasdi yinogvne yogotlvse tlasquu ama digaluga yigehe aseni osda tsigelihv.
segments.translation: Sometimes some of us would play in the woods. I thought everything was so pretty. When it was time to go to school I would say that I was sick. I just wanted to go out into the woods. I thought we were doing pretty good. We didn't have a bathroom or running water, but I thought it was good.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: I guess you all weren't starving.

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
segments.text: ᎾᏛ ᎤᏛᎯᏍᏓ ᏌᏕᎦ ᏥᏚᏙᎥ ᎤᏔᏂ ᏣᏫᏏᏍᎬ. ᎠᎿᏛᎮ ᎠᎵᏍᏓᏴᏗ ᏦᏥᎩᏍᎬ ᏦᏣᎵᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎦ. ᎠᎿᏛ ᏒᎯᏰ ᏗᏢ ᏱᏩᎩᏴᏟ ᎠᎿᏃᏩ ᎦᏚ ᏦᏩᏢᏅ ᏱᏓᏝ. ᏍᎩᎾ ᏳᏓᎭ peanut butter ᏃᎴ mustard ᏥᎨᎲ. Huh-uh Ꮭ...?
segments.transliteration: nadv udvhisda sadega tsidudov utani tsawisisgv. ahnadvhe alisdayvdi tsotsigisgv tsotsalisdayvhvsga. ahnadv svhiye ditlv yiwagiyvtli ahnanowa gadu tsowatlvnv yidatla. sgina yudaha peanut butter nole mustard tsigehv. Huh-uh tla...?
segments.translation: There was a guy named Sadeg and he had a really big garden. We got our food there so we could eat. When I would go into her house, she would have biscuits there. Sometimes I would put peanut butter or mustard on it.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Who was close by?

segments.speaker: naomi-stone
